title: ddPCR for Probes to Target eDNA Samples
author: Marine Vautier
materials: Pre and post extraction equipment decontamination: - Specific DNA-workstation: UV decontamination. Turn on the following equipments: - the QX200 droplet generator - the PX1 PCR plate sealer at 180 °C - the thermal cycler for PCR - the QX600 or QX200 droplet reader for ddPCR Tubes annotation - One 0.5 mL / 1.5 mL / 2 mL or 5 mL tube for the reaction mix according to the number of samples to be analysed. - PCR strips: 8 samples per PCR strip.

steps.title: Prepare plate layout and load samples
steps.instruction: Collect DNA samples, negative and positive controls from the freezer and defrost them for 10 min at 4 °C; vortex and briefly benchtop‑centrifuge each sample; take DNase/RNase‑free water for the NTC; according to the plate layout pipette the required volume of each DNA sample or control into the corresponding well of a PCR strip (maximum 6 µL DNA per 20 µL reaction for rare targets, dilute abundant samples e.g., 1/100); close the strip, annotate it, and store at –20 °C if the ddPCR will be performed the next day or at 4 °C if it will be performed immediately.

steps.title: Calculate and prepare reaction mix
steps.instruction: Calculate reagent volumes for the number of reactions (Table 2); prepare a total mix volume of 22 µL per reaction (20 µL final reaction plus a 2 µL pipetting margin); defrost the supermix at room temperature, primers, probe, water and buffer at 4 °C (keep the restriction enzyme frozen until needed and use it only when DNA exceeds 66 ng per reaction); vortex and briefly centrifuge all reagents, vortex the supermix thoroughly to eliminate any concentration gradient; add the reagents to a tube one‑by‑one, vortex and briefly centrifuge the completed mix; cover the tube with aluminium foil and keep at room temperature for immediate dispensing or at 4 °C for a few hours.

steps.title: Dispense reaction mix into PCR strips
steps.instruction: If the PCR strips were frozen, defrost them for 10 min at 4 °C, then vortex and briefly centrifuge; vortex the prepared reaction mix and briefly centrifuge; pipette the appropriate volume of mix into each well (e.g., 19 µL when 3 µL DNA is added); cover the strips with aluminium foil and place at 4 °C if the samples are prone to thermal degradation, otherwise leave at room temperature; allow the strips to stand at room temperature for at least 3 min before loading into the cartridge.

steps.title: Generate droplets in DG8 cartridge
steps.instruction: Within one hour of the previous step, place a DG8 cartridge into its holder, vortex and briefly centrifuge all PCR strips, dispense 20 µL of the DNA‑sample + reaction‑mix mixture into the cartridge middle line and 70 µL droplet‑generation oil into the bottom line (tilt the pipette 15° and stop the plunger after the first stop to avoid bubbles); place a DG8 gasket on the cartridge, open the droplet generator by pressing the green button, insert the cartridge, press the button again to close and start droplet generation; when the three indicator lights turn green, remove the cartridge and discard the gasket.

steps.title: Transfer droplets to 96‑well plate and seal
steps.instruction: Using a multi‑channel pipette, slowly draw 40 µL of droplets from the cartridge top line (tip at the bottom, hold the pipette at a 30‑45° angle; ~5 s), then dispense into the corresponding well of a ddPCR 96‑well plate (tip near the side of the well, ~5 s); repeat for all samples, keeping the plate on ice or at room temperature until all wells are filled; cover the plate with a pierceable foil seal (coloured line on top) and seal at 180 °C for 5 s with a plate sealer; verify that all wells are sealed; the sealed plate should be thermally cycled within 30 min or can be stored at 4 °C for up to 4 h before cycling.

steps.title: Thermal cycle the sealed plate
steps.instruction: Place the sealed ddPCR 96‑well plate into the PCR thermal cycler, program the cycling conditions (Table 3) using a 2.5 °C/s ramp rate, do not exceed 50 cycles, and adjust annealing/extension as needed; start the PCR run; after completion the plate may be stored up to 24 h before reading.

steps.title: Run droplet reader analysis
steps.instruction: Turn on the droplet reader (QX200 or QX600) and place the plate on the reader support; open the reader (green button) and insert the support; launch the associated software, check oil and waste‑bin levels (error message appears if replacement is needed), prime a new oil bottle if installed, and flush the system if the instrument has not been used for >1 month; define the experiment: add plate & configure plate, load or create a plate template, name the plate and select the appropriate supermix plate information; select wells to analyse and click “Include selected wells”; optionally enter target name, fluorescence channel and sample type (default “Unknown”) and click “Apply”; click “Start Run”, confirm, and monitor the analysis time; results are displayed live and saved automatically in the dedicated folder.
